title: Cross-browser testing and progressive enhancement
learningObjectives: Explain cross-browser testing and progressive enhancement and implement a maintainable CSS workflow or lab.

understand.concept: Cross-browser testing checks the interface in the browsers and versions relevant to the audience. Progressive enhancement starts with robust content and baseline styles, then adds features when supported. Feature queries and well-chosen fallbacks help manage differences.
understand.whyItMatters: Browser support tables cannot replace testing the actual user journey. Test layout, keyboard interaction, fonts, forms, media, and reduced-motion preferences in representative browsers and devices.
understand.analogy: Progressive enhancement is like building a reliable base before adding optional improvements.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the design; implementation must follow browser APIs, CSS behaviour, and accessibility requirements.

explain.narrative: The baseline content and padding remain. Grid is an enhancement for browsers that report support.

practise.guidedTask: Prepare a short browser test matrix for your page. Verify baseline content, responsive layout, focus states, and any feature-query enhancements.
practise.independentTask: Build a small production-minded example. Validate input, keep the baseline usable, and document browser and accessibility checks.

Use textContent for user-generated output rather than unsafe HTML insertion.

questions.prompt: What is the starting point of progressive enhancement?
questions.explanation: Progressive enhancement begins with core content and functionality before optional enhancements.
